observations: All three photos show the same disassembled engine block/assembly resting on a paved/tiled surface outdoors.
The word 'PORSCHE' is embossed on the black plastic engine cover in photos 0, 1, and 2.
Engine appears to be a V-configuration (V6/V8 style) with intake manifold, throttle body, wiring harness, and pulley/belt system visible.
Valve cover area on the left side (photos 0, 1) shows heavy brown/tan residue consistent with oil seepage or old oil buildup.
Several hoses and wiring connectors are disconnected and dangling (photo 1, bottom; photo 2, top), suggesting the engine was pulled and is incomplete or stripped of ancillaries.
A worn fan belt/serpentine belt lies loose near the bottom of the engine in photo 0.
Background shows a repair yard setting: plastic chair with a seated person, wheelbarrow tire, metal cart frame, and paving stones — consistent with an informal spare-parts yard in Abuja.
A watermark reading 'EZE PORSCHE GLOBAL AUTOS' is overlaid on all three images.
No VIN plate, engine code sticker, or part number is visible or legible in any photo.
No photo shows the engine running, on a test stand, or with compression/leak-down test results.

claims.claim: We also deals in all kinds of car spare parts
claims.evidence: General business claim about the seller's inventory; no photo can confirm scope of stock beyond the single engine shown.

risks.risk: Engine may not run or may have internal faults (compression, bearings, timing) since it is shown static and disconnected.
risks.proof: A video clip of the engine starting and idling, or a compression test report with engine code visible.

risks.risk: Heavy residue on valve cover and seals suggests possible oil leak or past overheating/burning.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the valve cover gasket area and oil pan after cleaning, showing no active leak.
risks.if_unproven: priced as having a leak, factored into worst-case cost

risks.risk: Dangling, cut, or disconnected wiring harness and sensors indicate the engine may be missing ECU, sensors, or wiring loom needed for installation.
risks.proof: Full photo of the complete wiring harness and ECU included with the engine, laid out separately.

risks.risk: No engine code or VIN tag visible, so exact Porsche model/displacement/year cannot be confirmed, which affects compatibility and value tier.
risks.proof: Clear photo of the engine code stamp/plate or a VIN-matched invoice.
risks.if_unproven: priced at the lowest tier for an unidentified Porsche V-engine family

risks.risk: Mileage/usage history of the engine (e.g., from an accident-damaged car vs. normal teardown) is unknown.
risks.proof: Photo of the donor vehicle or a teardown/removal video.

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the engine code/serial plate stamped on the block.
A start-up video showing the engine running and idling.
Photo of all included ancillary parts (ECU, wiring harness, sensors) laid out together.
Close-up of valve cover gasket/seal area to assess leak condition.
Photo or document of the donor vehicle (chassis plate or registration) to confirm engine origin.
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable as a used Porsche V-type engine by the visible branding, but with no engine code, no running demonstration, and visible leak residue plus disconnected wiring, it must be priced at worst case as an untested, possibly incomplete pulled engine.
